title: 98 dead, then a reckoning: how Florida's post-Surfside condo laws are landing on owners
dek: Mandatory milestone inspections, reserve rules owners can no longer vote away, and six-figure special assessments. What the law actually says, and what it's costing buildings across the state.
author: Charlie Triantafilou
image_alt: The partially collapsed Champlain Towers South in Surfside at night, June 2021

title: The holdouts who beat a developer in court, and lost their building anyway
dek: Biscayne 21's owners won at the Third District Court of Appeal. A reported $50 million settlement later, the 1964 tower is set to come down for a 55-story luxury project.
author: Charlie Triantafilou
image_alt: Edgewater neighborhood towers along Biscayne Bay, Miami

title: $1.6 million became $36 million: inside the Galleon's oceanfront assessment fight
dek: Owners at a Galt Ocean Mile condo report assessments of $135,000 to $320,000 per unit after five years of repairs. The contractor says the owners approved the bigger scope.
author: Charlie Triantafilou
image_alt: Aerial view of the Fort Lauderdale beachfront

title: A $21 million assessment, a board ousted, and now a lawsuit: 1060 Brickell takes on its contractor
dek: The association behind two 45-story Brickell towers says its contractor overbilled and filed "willfully exaggerated" liens. The contractor did not respond to reporters.
author: Charlie Triantafilou
